risks.note: BRSR discloses a permanent-employee turnover rate of 75.28% in FY 2025-26 (male 77.40%, female 69.16%) versus 74.10% in FY 2024-25 and 89.50% in FY 2023-24 - i.e. roughly three-quarters of the workforce turns over every year and the rate worsened year-on-year. The MD&A SWOT (routed to the strategy bundle) names 'High frontline attrition in labour-intensive IFM' and 'skill gaps in specialized areas like technical maintenance, and medical service solutions', requiring ongoing training/upskilling investment. With ~56,252 permanent employees, recruitment and training capacity is a structural cost and a delivery-continuity risk.
risks.risk: Extreme frontline attrition in a labour-intensive service model

risks.note: The MD&A internal-controls section reproduces the auditors' exception: the audit trail (edit log) was NOT enabled at the database layer for the entire audit period; not enabled at the application layer from 1 April 2025 to 18 November 2025; and from 19 November 2025 to 31 March 2026 not enabled for certain fields of tables for payroll, procurement, revenue, property plant and equipment and financial reporting; nor for changes made by users with privileged/debug access. This is a live control gap over the highest-risk processes for a payroll-heavy business. It sits alongside three Chief Financial Officers holding office within FY26 (Radha Ramanujan until 04-09-2025, Surinder Kumar until 16-03-2026, Ram Praveen from 16-03-2026 - per the related-party KMP list in the governance bundle) and the Chairman's reference to 'addressing certain internal matters that called for decisive leadership and focused attention' during FY 2025-26 (Chairman's message, profile bundle).
risks.risk: Internal financial control weakness: accounting-software audit trail not enabled, plus rapid CFO turnover

risks.note: BRSR Principle 1 discloses a monetary penalty imposed by the CJM, Ernakulam after a Labour Inspector inspected a CLIENT's site, observed non-compliance and filed a criminal complaint against UDS for breaches of the Act; no appeal was preferred. Because the workforce is deployed inside client premises under client-specific SOPs, compliance failures at customer sites convert into prosecutions and penalties against UDS. The Company also has to police statutory dues of value-chain partners (it obtains remittance challans as proof). Evolving labour codes are flagged by management as both an opportunity and a compliance burden.
risks.risk: Statutory/labour-law liability arising at customers' premises

risks.note: BRSR states 100% of turnover comes from one described business activity - 'Support services to Organizations / Housekeeping & Maintenance Service' (NIC 82990) - with exports contributing just 0.09% of turnover and operations in 27 states and only 2 countries. The MD&A SWOT (strategy bundle) separately flags 'Regional Revenue Tilt: Heavier reliance on South India ... necessitating broader national penetration'. There is no customer-concentration disclosure in the routed text either way.

The MD&A SWOT (strategy bundle) flags 'elevated debtor days from large-project mobilizations' that strain cash flows, and 'prudent provisioning (e.g., Avon logistics receivables)' that temporarily compressed profitability - management explicitly links profitability to one-off operational lapses 'despite strengthened controls'. The Board's Report attributes weaker FY26 profitability to cost pressures, growth investments and revenue-mix changes.

Management flags that 'Increased Industry Fragmentation would lead to margins to further fall due to increased pricing pressure and unviable contracts', and that 'Highly fragmented markets limit pricing power; unorganized players and new entrants could erode share without superior execution' (SWOT, strategy bundle). Wage-code pass-through is cited as a partial mitigant.
risks.risk: Fragmented, price-competitive market limiting pricing power

risks.note: Management flags that 'Rapid AI adoption risks commoditizing routine services (voice bots in Athena/Denave), necessitating continuous innovation to avoid client in-sourcing', and that global IT slowdowns and hiring freezes could prolong softness in BSS sub-segments such as employee background checks and demand generation - the same sub-segments the SWOT calls volatile because of IT hiring slowdown and client-mix shifts (strategy bundle).
risks.risk: Technology disruption / client in-sourcing and BSS demand softness

risks.note: BRSR reports 22 total recordable work-related injuries in FY 2025-26 (24 in FY 2024-25) and 22 high-consequence work-related injuries or ill health, with zero fatalities in both years; employee LTIFR improved to 1.03 per million person-hours from 5.38. Only 90% of plants/offices were assessed for health-and-safety practices and working conditions, and value-chain partner assessment covered 95% (H&S) and 80% (working conditions), leaving an unassessed tail. Note the internal inconsistency that 'total recordable work-related injuries' and 'high-consequence injuries' are reported at identical values (22 / 24), which is implausible as normally reported.
risks.risk: Workforce health-and-safety exposure at deployed sites
